docsBody: The local search index was still building or could not run — typically when the POS tab has been in the background or another tab holds the database lead. Searches still answer, from a direct scan of the local catalogue, and switch back to the index automatically once it responds. No catalogue data was changed.
troubleshooting: Usually no action is needed: search results keep working and the index takes over again on its own.
If this code appears on every search all day, keep the POS in its own browser window rather than a background tab, and reload the app once.
If the code returns after a reload, export debug info and contact support; the log context identifies the affected catalogue.
evidence: monorepo#1733 silent zero-result searches while the index pipeline was stalled

actionHint: No action needed. If search still misses products you can see in the catalogue, reload the app.
summary: The search index could not find a product it should contain; the app attempts an automatic search index rebuild.
docsBody: A periodic self-check asked the local search index for a product by that product's own name and the index did not return it. That means searches may have been showing fewer results than the catalogue really holds. The app attempts to rebuild the local search index automatically. No catalogue data was changed.
troubleshooting: Usually no action is needed: the index is rebuilt automatically and searches recover on their own.
If search still misses products you can see in the catalogue, reload the app to rebuild the in-memory index.
If the code returns, export debug info and contact support; the log context identifies the affected catalogue and the sample the index missed.
evidence: monorepo#1733 divergence detector was one-sided: false hits were detected, false misses never were

actionHint: Try another search; reload if results still look wrong.
summary: A search index rebuild failed, so results may be incomplete while the app retries initialization.
docsBody: After detecting a search index problem the app tried to rebuild the index, and the rebuild itself failed. Search keeps answering — from the existing index with known bad results hidden, or from a direct scan of the data on this device — but it may miss or misrank results for the affected list. The next search or readiness check retries index initialization and can recover automatically; reloading the app is an optional fresh start if results remain wrong. No store data was changed.
troubleshooting: Open the log entry — its context names the list affected and the error the rebuild hit. If that error mentions storage, free up space on the device first; on web, also avoid private/incognito windows.
Run another search on the affected list; the app will retry index initialization automatically.
If results are still missing or wrongly ordered, reload the app (or browser tab). If CLIENT144 is logged again, export debug info and contact support.
evidence: 2026-09-01 log audit: both rebuild-failure paths from monorepo#1733 logged without a code while their sibling detections carried CLIENT141-143

actionHint: Remove that line and add it again, then check the total.
summary: A line on this order has price details the POS could not read, so its amount was taken from the stored totals instead.
docsBody: The line's saved price basis — the price, tax status and tax-inclusive flag the POS records against it — could not be read, so the amount shown was derived from whatever totals were already on the line. Remove the line and add it again to rebuild that data, then check the order total before taking payment.
troubleshooting: Check the order total against what you expect before taking payment — the affected line's amount came from stored totals, not from a recalculated price.
Remove the affected line and add the product, fee or shipping method again; a freshly added line always carries readable price details.
If the line was added on an older version of WCPOS, or restored from a backup, the price details it carries may predate the current format — re-adding it is the fix.
If new lines keep producing this code, export debug info and contact support with the order number: something is writing the POS price data in a format the app cannot read.

actionHint: Check the tax on this order; ask the admin whether a tax rate was deleted.
summary: This order refers to a tax rate your store no longer has, so its tax may be wrong.
docsBody: A line on the order carries a tax rate id that is not in the store's current tax tables — usually because the rate was deleted or edited in WooCommerce after the order was started. Check the tax on the order before taking payment, and have whoever manages the store confirm the tax rates.
troubleshooting: Check the tax amount on the order before taking payment — the rate it was calculated with is no longer in your store.
Ask whoever manages the store whether a tax rate was deleted or edited recently; deleting a rate that orders already reference is the usual cause.
Start the sale on a new order once the tax rates are settled — a new order picks up the store's current rates.
If the store's tax rates have not changed, the POS may be holding a stale copy: open Store health and resync tax rates, then export debug info and contact support if the code returns.

actionHint: Keep using the till; the display retries on the next cart change.
summary: The customer display could not build the cart snapshot; the display shows the idle screen until the next change.
docsBody: The till keeps working while the customer display shows the idle screen. The display tries to build the cart snapshot again when the cart changes.
troubleshooting: The till keeps working; only the customer display returns to the idle screen until the cart changes.
If this repeats, report the affected order and include exported debug info.

actionHint: The cash is in the drawer but not in your store — retry it from the register panel before you count.
summary: Your store refused a paid in, paid out or no sale that the till has already recorded.
docsBody: The cash has physically moved and the till knows about it, but your store does not. Retry the movement from the register panel; if it keeps failing, note the amount and reason before you close, because the store's expected total will be short or over by exactly that amount.
troubleshooting: Open the register panel. A refused movement is listed at the top of the pane with a Retry button — retry it first, because most refusals are a permission or session problem rather than the amount.
If the log entry names a field, that field is what your store rejected. Record the movement again with a valid amount and a reason.

If it keeps failing, write the amount, type and reason down before counting: the store's expected total does not include this movement, so the drawer will read short (paid out) or over (paid in) by that amount.
A refusal on every movement usually means the cashier's account lost the Manage cash capability, or the session was closed on another device. Check both in WP Admin.
Do not close the register until the movement has either gone through or been written down — the till keeps the row, but it is the only copy.

actionHint: The original movement still stands in your store — check it before recording anything else.
summary: Your store would not reverse a cash movement, so the original one still counts.
docsBody: The till shows the movement as reversed; your store still counts it. The usual causes are a movement that was already reversed, or one that belongs to a session that has since been counted.
troubleshooting: Check the register panel's paid in / out list: the movement the reversal was aimed at is the one your store still counts.
A movement can only be reversed once, and only while its session is open — after counting starts, your store refuses reversals by design.
If the reversal was a mistake, nothing needs doing: the store never applied it.
If the reversal was correct and your store still refuses it, record a matching opposite movement instead so the drawer and the store agree.

actionHint: Sales are still safe, but they are not attached to a till session — reopen the register.
summary: Your store refused to open this register session, so nothing is being counted against it.
docsBody: Selling still works and no order is at risk, but this device's register session does not exist in your store. Cash movements cannot be recorded against it and the session will not appear in the register reports.
troubleshooting: Close and reopen the register from the register panel — a fresh session usually opens cleanly.
If the log entry names a field, the opening float is the usual culprit: re-enter it as plain digits with a single decimal point.
**Store admin:** confirm the register still exists and is not retired in WP Admin, and that the cashier's account has the Manage cash capability.
Orders taken while no session exists are saved normally but carry no session, so they will not appear in that shift's register report.

actionHint: Write the counted figures down before reopening — the till does not keep them.
summary: Your store refused this register's count, so the session is still open there.
docsBody: Your store turned the close down rather than missing it, so nothing retries it. The register goes back to showing Open register, and the till does not keep the count through that: when it rejoins the session its copy of the figures is replaced by the store’s, which has none. Write down what you counted before touching the register again.
troubleshooting: Write down what you counted — notes, cash and each other tender — before touching the register again.
Fix the cause first, or the next attempt is refused the same way. The usual ones are the closing cashier losing permission to manage cash, and a session already closed on another device.
If the close needed a manager’s approval, that approval is checked at the moment of the close and does not carry over; ask for it again on the new attempt.
Reopen the register. The store still has this shift open, so the till rejoins the existing session rather than starting a second one, and the original opening float and cashier are shown.
Count again from the figures you wrote down, and close.

actionHint: Another device holds this register — check which drawer you are actually counting.
summary: Another device already had this register open, so this till joined that session instead of starting its own.
docsBody: Two devices opened the same register. Your store keeps the session that was already open and this device has switched to it, so both tills now count the same drawer. Anything this device recorded before switching belongs to the session it abandoned.
troubleshooting: Check the opening float and the cashier shown in the register panel: they are now the other device's, not the ones typed here.
Two tills on one register means one physical drawer counted by two people — agree who is counting before the shift ends, or give each device its own register.
Any cash movement recorded on this device before the switch stayed with the abandoned session and is not in the drawer total you can now see.
**Store admin:** the register list in WP Admin shows which sessions are open and on which register.

actionHint: Ask a different manager to approve the count, then close again.
summary: Your store would not accept the manager approval for this count, so the register is still open.
docsBody: The count is held on this device and nothing is lost. Your store refuses an approval when the password is wrong, when the approver is the same person who is closing, or when that account cannot approve closes.
troubleshooting: Check the username and password — an approval is a normal WordPress sign-in and is case sensitive.
A cashier cannot approve their own count: the approver must be a different account from the one closing the register.
The approving account needs permission to manage register closures. A shop manager has it by default; a cashier does not.
**Store admin:** repeated refusals on one till are worth looking at. Each attempt is recorded, and a short drawer with several failed approvals is the pattern worth investigating.

actionHint: Close the error message to retry; if it comes back, reload the app.
summary: Part of the screen failed to load and was replaced by an error message.
docsBody: A screen or panel hit an error while drawing, so WCPOS replaced it with an error message instead of closing. The rest of the app keeps working, and the failure itself wrote and lost nothing: it is a defect in the app, not a problem with your store. The log entry carries the error and the component that failed, which is what support needs; when error reporting is allowed the same failure reaches the developers automatically.
troubleshooting: Close the error message (the X) — the panel redraws, and a one-off failure clears on its own.
If it comes straight back, reload the app: reload the browser tab on web, or close and reopen the app on desktop and mobile.
If the same message returns after a reload, export debug info from the Logs screen and contact support — the entry names the error and the component that failed.
evidence: monorepo#2112 — a Windows till blocked at login behind a boundary-caught error that produced no Sentry event in 90 days

actionHint: Choose the store again to sign back in. If the site had to be added again, contact support before clearing local data.
summary: The saved store session was incomplete, so WCPOS returned to the store list.
docsBody: WCPOS remembers which site, cashier and store were open so the till can resume where it left off. This time part of that record was missing — usually the site or cashier entry — so instead of opening the store with a broken session the till returned to the store list. Only the pointer to the open session was cleared; the store’s local data stays on the device. Choosing the same store again picks it up. If the site had to be added again, the till opens a fresh local copy of the store, and sales still waiting to sync under the previous session are not picked up automatically — contact support before clearing local data. A repeat on one device means its local storage is not keeping what the app writes.
troubleshooting: Choose the site and store again to sign back in — the store’s data on this device is untouched; only the remembered session was cleared.

If the site is no longer in the list, enter its address again and sign in. Contact support first if you know sales were still waiting to sync: a re-added site opens a fresh local copy of the store and does not pick the old one up.
If it happens again on the same device, its local storage is not keeping what the app writes: check free disk space, and look at the Logs screen for storage errors from around the same time.
Export debug info and contact support if it keeps recurring — the log entry names which part of the session was missing.
evidence: monorepo#2112 — 2026-09-16 Spanish Windows till stuck on 'useStoreSession must be called within an active store session' after a main-process storage failure (wcpos/electron#459)
